⚠️ [IMPORTANT] `replace(",", "")` strips commas from anywhere in the cell, so values that used to fail loudly now sum to a silently wrong total with exit 0. Verified on this head: `1.234,56` → `1.23` (~1000× off), `1,3` → `13.00`, `12,34,5` → `12345.00`. Each of those previously raised `TallyError` naming the row. For a tool whose output finance reconciles against, a wrong number at exit 0 is worse than the original failure — and invariant 28 of `specs/4-group-by-and-format/PRODUCT.md` pins exit 0 to a trustworthy result.

Strip commas only when they form well-formed thousands groups, and let anything else keep hitting the existing `ValueError` path:

```suggestion
                            numeral = cell.removeprefix("$")
                            integer, _, fraction = numeral.lstrip("+-").partition(".")
                            chunks = integer.split(",")
                            if "," in numeral and not (
                                "," not in fraction
                                and all(c.isdigit() for c in chunks)
                                and 1 <= len(chunks[0]) <= 3
                                and all(len(c) == 3 for c in chunks[1:])
                            ):
                                raise ValueError(numeral)
                            value = float(numeral.replace(",", ""))
```

Validated in a scratch copy of this branch: `uv run pytest -q` still passes 38/38; `$1,234.56`, `$12.00`, `1,234,567.89`, `-1,234.56` and `1234.56` all parse, while `1.234,56`, `1,3`, `12,34,5` and `,234` exit 1 with the row number. A module-level `re.fullmatch` is equally fine if you prefer it — the ask is the validation, not this mechanism. Please also add a case to `tests/test_total.py` asserting one malformed-comma cell is still rejected; nothing currently covers that path.

<!-- factory:review -->

Fixed in 159c829: only strip a comma when it forms a well-formed thousands group (1-3 leading digits, then groups of exactly 3, no comma in the fractional part), via a `_THOUSANDS` regex checked before `float()`. Anything else — `1.234,56`, `1,3`, `12,34,5`, `,234` — now still raises `TallyError` naming the row, same as before this fix existed. `$1,234.56`, `$12.00`, `1,234,567.89`, `-1,234.56`, and plain `1234.56` all continue to parse correctly.

Added `test_total_rejects_a_malformed_comma_grouping` covering the European-decimal-comma case; `uv run pytest -q` passes 39/39 (38 previous + 1 new). Also manually re-verified every counterexample listed in this thread plus the original reporter scenario against the new code.

Used a module-level `re.fullmatch`-style check (your suggested mechanism was fine too) for readability inline with the rest of the file.
